strategies.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Because of its passivity, Jumpluff requires partners that deal meaningful damage on their own to foes; this means that they will likely need to have spread moves such as Heat Wave to damage both foes at once.
  • Pokemon that set up with either boosting moves or other options like Trick Room appreciate Jumpluff's ability to redirect attacks or shut down foes altogether with Sleep Powder.
  • Jumpluff heavily appreciates allies with Drought, as it makes it so that Jumpluff isn't forced to waste a turn setting up the sun for itself with Sunny Day.
  • Charizard is a great offensive ally for Jumpluff, using Heat Wave to damage foes and appreciating Jumpluff's access to Sunny Day and Rage Powder, activating Charizard's Solar Power and protecting the frail threat from powerful attacks, respectively.
  • Torkoal can damage both foes with Eruption and sets up the sun for Jumpluff. Jumpluff can additionally use Pollen Puff to heal Torkoal to fire off a more powerful Eruption.
  • Ursaluna is another ally that can consistently damage foes with spread moves, this time with Earthquake, which is able to be used freely next to Jumpluff thanks to its Ground immunity. In return, Jumpluff can put foes to sleep, namely Sneasler, before they can move so Ursaluna is free to attack. Jumpluff can also redirect attacks or disrupt foes with Encore to ensure that Ursaluna's Flame Orb activates safely. Jumpluff, when used with faster Ursaluna sets, can use Tailwind to allow Ursaluna to outspeed a significant portion of the unboosted metagame.
  • Jumpluff is very supportive and cannot do any meaningful damage on its own. It is particularly useless in front of Gholdengo or Pokemon with Safety Goggles such as Incineroar, as they can ignore Jumpluff entirely or KO it with Make It Rain and Flare Blitz, respectively. Allies such as Charizard and Hisuian Typhlosion are able to break through many of these Pokemon with their devastating attacks. Jumpluff also has a pretty poor defensive typing, being weak to top Pokemon such as Alolan Ninetales and Sneasler. Allies such as Incineroar can help out by threatening them with Flare Blitz or mitigating their damage with Intimidate, respectively. Jumpluff can also outspeed them with Drought support from Torkoal, putting them to sleep with Sleep Powder before they can threaten Jumpluff.

Strategy Comments

  • Jumpluff's main objective is to be a nuisance under then sun, putting foes to sleep, changing the Speed order with Tailwind, and resetting sun if necessary. Jumpluff loves to be in scenarios where it can spam Sleep Powder easily without worry. To help it achieve this, roadblocks such as powder-immune Pokemon like Safety Goggles Clefable and Rillaboom and sleep-immune Pokemon like Magmar and Electabuzz should be removed early on.
  • Jumpluff tends to prefer being brought in the front, getting off early Sleep Powders that could easily sway the battle in Jumpluff's favor. Jumpluff can be brought in many matchups, but certainly not Trick Room; because of its relatively poor bulk and lack of Protect, it won't be able to survive.
  • Jumpluff accentuates its potential in matchups against opposing weather teams, namely rain teams, as it can shut down their weather with Sunny Day before they can move. Additionally, Jumpluff can lock common rain Pokemon like Pelipper and Ursaluna into Protect with Encore, or it can redirect powerful Water-type attacks like Wave Crash from Basculegion away, protecting allies like Incineroar and Charizard.
  • Shutting down the sun with Pokemon such as Pelipper and Alolan Ninetales will sever Jumpluff's Speed boost, leaving it vulnerable to Pokemon such as Sneasler. Removing weather setters early-game and preserving Jumpluff's allies such as Torkoal will ensure that Jumpluff's preferred weather will be up. Jumpluff is also susceptible to Taunt from the likes of Whimsicott and Annihilape, considering most of its options are status moves. To counter this, removing the Taunt users early with explosive damage in the form of Charizard or Ursaluna will be helpful.

movesets.name: Sun Support
movesets.description:
• Jumpluff is a sun staple, providing fast and invaluable support in the form of speed control and sleep, among others.
  • Sunny Day is a good option because of Jumpluff's high Speed, letting it reliably override opposing weather before anything moves while boosting the power of allies such as Charizard. Rage Powder is the preferred last option, keeping frail allies like the aforementioned Charizard safe by redirecting away opposing attacks such as Wave Crash from Basculegion. Encore, on the other hand, punishes passive play like Fake Out and Protect. Pollen Puff can heal up allies like Ursaluna while also giving it an attacking move, making sure that Jumpluff isn't entirely useless when Taunted. Leaf Storm is a more offensive option, allowing Jumpluff to hit foes such as Ursaluna-B, Tera Water Gholdengo, and Basculegion in a pinch.
  • Covert Cloak blocks Fake Out from the likes of Rillaboom, letting Jumpluff continue to support its team without disturbance.
  • Tera Water flips Jumpluff's weaknesses to Fire- and Ice-type attacks such as Flare Blitz from Incineroar and Blizzard from Alolan Ninetales into resistances while granting a resistance to Make It Rain from Gholdengo, boosting its longevity.
  • The bulk lets Jumpluff survive Draco Meteor from Life Orb Hydreigon, Overheat from Magmar when not in the sun, 4 hits of Scale Shot from Dragonite, and almost always avoids a 2HKO from Iron Head from +1 Kingambit. The Speed investment lets Jumpluff always outspeed Adamant Sneasler.
  • Especially when the sun is active, Jumpluff is able to very easily outspeed a lot of threats such as Sneasler and put them to sleep. After that, however, Jumpluff relies entirely on its partners to deal damage, leaving it very easy to ignore and its partner vulnerable to being double targetted. This can be taken further with moves like Taunt, which removes Jumpluff's ability to attempt to save its partner with moves such as Rage Powder and Sleep Powder.
